html:
SMTO-GWT-0041 — This computer isn't set up to run local AI models

GUID: cc0d67f0-6cd4-4850-a83d-a4e1484bdc6f
Slug: managed-llm-disabled
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO asked this computer to start or manage a local AI model, but its Gateway has that feature switched off. It is off by default on Windows and Mac computers. Nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If another computer runs your local models, select it with the Target button below the message box and send the request again. Only Gateways with local model support switched on can start or manage models.
  2. To use this computer, ask the person who installed its Gateway to switch on its local model support and restart that Gateway. This option is set when the Gateway starts, so SMTO can't switch it on from here.
  3. After the Gateway restarts, select Check connection for it in Settings › Setup › Gateways, then ask SMTO again. A fresh check makes sure SMTO sees the Gateway's new setup before sending the request.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts the model or shows its status on that computer instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed that computer's Gateway. Don't try to start the model on that computer some other way while SMTO reports the feature as switched off.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused a managed model operation (local AI runtime or legacy /llm start, stop, status or log) with 501 because enable_llm_runtime is off in its startup profile.

What this means

  • The service checked enable_llm_runtime and found that the Gateway's managed model runtime was disabled in its startup profile. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The service checked enable_llm_runtime and found that the Gateway's managed model runtime was disabled in its startup profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway's effective startup profile and whether managed local model service is intended on that host.

How to fix it

  • Enable the managed model runtime in that Gateway's startup configuration (GATEWAY_ENABLE_LLM_RUNTIME=1; it defaults on only for Linux) and restart the Gateway, or route the request to a Gateway that advertises the llm_runtime/local AI capability. Do not bypass the check (gateway_core/service.py _ensure_llm_runtime_enabled).
  • Use a Gateway with the managed LLM capability or configure the supported Gateway startup options on that host.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway starts with the supported runtime option enabled and reports that capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
